subject: parameter table as first argument to simulateData()

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: parameter table as first argument to simulateData()
parts:
Hello,

I recently tried to put together a quick illustration of how effects can be attenuated by measurement error.  Rather than making separate syntax objects (one with population values for data generation, and one without for estimation), I made a single syntax object without parameter estimates, then used lavaanify() to make a parameter table.  I then place my population values in the parameter table's ustart vector, and used it as the first argument in the simulateData() function.  The following example produces a warning message:

library(lavaan)
set.seed(3141593)

myFLs <- seq(.4, .9, length.out = 6)
popParams <- c(rep(myFLs, 2), .5)
N <- 100

myModel <- "X =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6
  Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6
  Y ~ X
"
popModel <- lavaanify(myModel)
popModel$ustart <- popParams
popModel$unco <- 0
popModel$free <- 0
dat <- simulateData(popModel, model.type = "sem", fixed.x = FALSE, std.lv = TRUE,
                    return.type = "data.frame", sample.nobs = N, standardized = TRUE)

Error in data.frame(lhs = lhs, op = op, rhs = rhs, mod.idx = mod.idx,  : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 13, 0


Using debug(lavaanify), I found the error occurred when getLIST() was called.  Then using debug(lavaan:::getLIST), I found the error occurred here:

debug: USER <- data.frame(lhs = lhs, op = op, rhs = rhs, mod.idx = mod.idx,
                          stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
Error in data.frame(lhs = lhs, op = op, rhs = rhs, mod.idx = mod.idx,  :
   arguments imply differing number of rows: 13, 0

The mod.idx object remains NULL, when it was created from the FLAT$mod.idx vector (which was also NULL).  Leading up to that, I don't see a vector in FLAT that is called mod.idx, so I'm not sure that the problem didn't in fact start back in lavaanify().  Can you tell what the problem is, or whether I'm on the right track to find it?

Thanks,

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: parameter table as first argument to simulateData()
parts:
On 06/16/2013 10:28 PM, Terrence Jorgensen wrote:
> Hello,
>
> I recently tried to put together a quick illustration of how effects can
> be attenuated by measurement error. Rather than making separate syntax
> objects (one with population values for data generation, and one without
> for estimation), I made a single syntax object without parameter
> estimates, then used lavaanify() to make a parameter table. I then
> place my population values in the parameter table's ustart vector, and
> used it as the first argument in the simulateData() function.

Ok. That did not work, since simulataData() did not check if the input
was a parameter table or not (it assumed it was model syntax, called
lavaanify, and we got trouble). I guess you are the first to try this ;-)

This should be fixed in the dev version (0.5-14). But read on.

> library(lavaan)
> set.seed(3141593)
>
> myFLs <- seq(.4, .9, length.out = 6)
> popParams <- c(rep(myFLs, 2), .5)
> N <- 100
>
> myModel <- "X =~ x1 + x2 + x3 + x4 + x5 + x6
> Y =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4 + y5 + y6
> Y ~ X
> "
> popModel <- lavaanify(myModel)

This is not enough. You probably want:

popModel <- lavaanify(myModel, auto=TRUE, model.type="sem")

to add residuals, etc...

> popModel$ustart <- popParams

This will be slightly more complicated:

popModel$ustart[popModel$op == "=~"] <- rep(c(1, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7,
0.8), each=2)
popModel$ustart[popModel$op == "~"] <- 0.5

There is no need to do this. simulateData() does not care about
free/unco parameters. And if you must do this, you need to make sure the
entries are integers:

popModel$unco <- 0L
popModel$free <- 0L

> dat <- simulateData(popModel, model.type = "sem", fixed.x = FALSE,
> std.lv = TRUE,
> return.type = "data.frame", sample.nobs = N,
> standardized = TRUE)

Note that if you use standardized=TRUE, you should not use '1' as the
first factor loadings.

Yves.

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: parameter table as first argument to simulateData()
parts:
I'll also add that you can use ? as an operator in lavaan syntax to specify starting values (or population values for simulated data). See this example:

library(lavaan)

popModel <- "
    f1 =~ 1*y1 + 0.6*y2 + 0.7*y3
    f1 ~~ 0.8*f1
    y1 ~~ 0.5*y1
    y2 ~~ 1.1*y2
    y3 ~~ 0.8*y3
    "
 
popModel1 <- "
    f1 =~ 1*y1 + 0.6?y2 + 0.7?y3
    f1 ~~ 0.8?f1
    y1 ~~ 0.5?y1
    y2 ~~ 1.1?y2
    y3 ~~ 0.8?y3
    "
    
##Simulate with all fixed
set.seed(1234)
sim <- simulateData(popModel, model.type = "cfa", fixed.x = FALSE, return.type = "data.frame", sample.nobs = 100)

##Simulate with ? for starting values
set.seed(1234)
sim1 <- simulateData(popModel1, model.type = "cfa", fixed.x = FALSE, return.type = "data.frame", sample.nobs = 100)

##Are they the same? Yes, yes they are.
sim == sim1
